question: Hypothermia in a neonate can cause hypoglycaemia, because non-shivering thermogenesis (brown fat metabolism) rapidly depletes glucose stores when the neonate attempts to maintain body temperature in a cold environment.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. The statement is TRUE. Hypothermia triggers non-shivering thermogenesis via brown fat, which uses glucose → hypoglycaemia. The clinical implication is important: any cold neonate is at risk of hypoglycaemia, and vice versa. Always check blood glucose when treating hypothermia, and always check temperature when managing hypoglycaemia.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! Neonatal thermogenesis relies on brown adipose tissue (BAT) metabolism, which consumes glucose as a substrate. When a neonate is cold, BAT oxidation accelerates → glucose utilisation increases → hypoglycaemia develops, particularly in already-at-risk groups (preterm, SGA, IDM). This is why temperature AND glucose must always be measured together in a cold or symptomatic neonate.
